Findings.Description: Multiple overloads of Assert.That contain identical logic, leading to duplicated code and higher maintenance cost.
Findings.Recommendation: Consolidate the overloads by delegating to a single private helper that contains the shared implementation.
Findings.CodeSnippet: ConstraintEvaluator.Evaluate(code, expr, message, actualExpression, constraintExpression, ReportFailure);
Findings.QuickFix: Consolidate the overloads by delegating to a single private helper that contains the shared implementation.

Findings.Description: Method Evaluate has cyclomatic complexity well above the target of 10 due to multiple nested conditionals handling nulls, hook execution, and result processing.
Findings.Recommendation: Refactor Evaluate by extracting the hook handling, result evaluation, and failure reporting into separate private methods.
Findings.CodeSnippet: public static void Evaluate<T>(T actual, IResolveConstraint expr, ... )
Findings.QuickFix: Refactor Evaluate by extracting the hook handling, result evaluation, and failure reporting into separate private methods.

Findings.Description: The refactored Assert.That passes the expr argument directly to ConstraintEvaluator.Evaluate without checking for null, which could cause a NullReferenceException when expr.Resolve() is invoked inside Evaluate.
Findings.Recommendation: Add an ArgumentNullException check for expr before calling ConstraintEvaluator.Evaluate.
Findings.CodeSnippet: ConstraintEvaluator.Evaluate(code, expr, message, actualExpression, constraintExpression, ReportFailure);
Findings.QuickFix: Add an ArgumentNullException check for expr before calling ConstraintEvaluator.Evaluate.

Findings.Description: Warn.Until passes the expr argument to ConstraintEvaluator.Evaluate without null validation, risking a NullReferenceException if the caller supplies a null constraint expression.
Findings.Recommendation: Validate that expr is not null and throw ArgumentNullException before invoking ConstraintEvaluator.Evaluate.
Findings.CodeSnippet: ConstraintEvaluator.Evaluate(code, expr, message, actualExpression, constraintExpression, IssueUnlessWarning);
Findings.QuickFix: Validate that expr is not null and throw ArgumentNullException before invoking ConstraintEvaluator.Evaluate.

Findings.Description: TestActionCommand directly references the concrete TestMethod type, violating the Dependency Inversion Principle and reducing testability of the command.
Findings.Recommendation: Introduce an ITest interface abstraction and depend on it instead of the concrete TestMethod class.
Findings.CodeSnippet: Guard.ArgumentValid(innerCommand.Test is TestMethod, "TestActionCommand may only apply to a TestMethod", nameof(innerCommand));
Findings.QuickFix: Introduce an ITest interface abstraction and depend on it instead of the concrete TestMethod class.

Findings.Description: The static class name TestActionHookRunner does not clearly convey that it is responsible for invoking hooks around test actions; a more descriptive name would improve readability.
Findings.Recommendation: Rename TestActionHookRunner to TestActionHookExecutor to better reflect its purpose.
Findings.QuickFix: Rename TestActionHookRunner to TestActionHookExecutor to better reflect its purpose.
